A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CQN-AS study and contain complete, matching scientific material, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C. The added acknowledgements and shifted pagination in v5 do not limit comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original robot-control simulations, baseline comparisons, ablations and failure-case experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical outcomes, including the BiGym, RLBench and HumanoidBench results and the ablation studies.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendix C retain identical critic definitions, GRU architecture, training objectives, replay handling, coarse-to-fine inference and temporal-ensemble action execution.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 25 BiGym tasks, 20 RLBench tasks, eight HumanoidBench tasks and DeepMind Control Suite locomotion failure cases. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: CQN, DrQ-v2+ and ACT in Figures 5–6; SAC, TD3 and their action-sequence variants in Figure 2; and CQN and SAC in Figure 8.

E3.justification: Demonstration processing, observations, action modes, training budgets, metrics and BiGym/RLBench evaluations over 25 episodes match. Appendix B retains the same task configurations and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Figure 2's return-prediction and overestimation analyses are unchanged. Figure 7 retains the same sequence-length, RL-objective, N-step-return and temporal-ensemble ablations, including torque-control failure cases.

E5.justification: Run counts and mean/confidence-interval reporting match: eight runs for BiGym, four for RLBench and Figure 7, and eight CQN-AS/CQN runs versus three SAC runs in Appendix A.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 and 5–8 retain identical result plots, including curves and uncertainty bands. Associated numerical statements, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged, with no result entries added or removed.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, objectives and multidimensional formulations in Appendix C are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and Section 6 retain the same claims about action sequences improving value learning, CQN-AS avoiding overestimation and its robot-control performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications match. Both retain the limitations concerning real-world evaluation, delicate objects, reactive control and torque control in Sections 4 and 6.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical data-processing instructions, task and hyperparameter tables, hardware, runtimes and baseline implementation links. The project webpage disclosure is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the complete bibliography match after accounting for changed page breaks. No cited works or substantive relationships to prior research are added, removed or revised.

P1.justification: v5 adds a short Acknowledgements section before the references, providing contributor credit, funding information and an institutional-role disclosure. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements block pushes the references downward and reflows the bibliography onto an additional page. Appendices begin on page 14 instead of 13. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–4 retain their displays, captions and layouts.

improvement.justification: v5 adds contributor credit, ARO/MURI funding disclosure and clarification of Abbeel's UC Berkeley and Amazon roles that were absent from v4. These modestly improve attribution and transparency. The scientific content, empirical support, limitations and reproducibility information are unchanged.
